body.title: One common model for every artifact

summary.prose: Every thing insrc stores becomes the same kind of object, with an identity, a parent, a history, feedback from people, references to related things and a lifecycle that says where it stands. Tasks become first-class and can take feedback like anything else, tracker issues and stored artifacts stay in step, and there is one way to name things instead of two. Existing repositories are converted once, up front, so the delivery board and later signoff work see one consistent shape.

body.problem: Persisted entities share no common model. Each artifact type declares its own metadata, feedback, tracker links and citations [[c4]]; approval, review, revision and staleness are loose fields in each artifact's metadata; a Task exists only as a row inside a Plan, so it has no feedback, history or references of its own [[c4]]. Two identity schemes coexist, one for stored artifacts and a second for work items, and they have already drifted so the same epic carries two different ids [[c2]] [[c3]]. Human comments written on tracker issues are never read back, so a Task, the unit people actually work on, cannot take feedback [[c1]]. Because there is no uniform shape, the delivery board has to know every artifact type [[c5]], and the signoff and revision work planned for teams has nothing consistent to bind to [[c6]].

nonGoals.text: Changing how team signoff, revision handling or tracker status sync work (stories s7 to s9 of the team epic)
nonGoals.rationale: They depend on this model and are built afterwards; building them in the same Epic would couple two large changes [[c6]].

nonGoals.text: Turning a revision request into an automatic plan re-run or an automatic re-signoff
nonGoals.rationale: What a revision means for signoff belongs to the revision and signoff work, not to the data model [[c6]].

nonGoals.text: A team roster of identities in the central policy
nonGoals.rationale: Identities are declared per user for attribution; gates use the tracker's own identity, so a roster is not needed and can be added later [[c7]].

nonGoals.text: Behaviour of the future PRD artifact
nonGoals.rationale: Only the Define keeps its place above the Epic so a PRD can be added later; PRD behaviour is a separate Epic [[c7]].

nonGoals.text: Any change to the deprecated IDE repository
nonGoals.rationale: The IDE repository is deprecated and out of scope [[c7]].
Comments are read on demand and where the holder works on the unit; polling adds load and failure modes without a requirement [[c1]].

nonGoals.text: Migrating existing data one artifact at a time as it is touched
nonGoals.rationale: The delivery board reads every artifact, so a mix of old and new shapes would break it; migration is one upfront cutover [[c1]] [[c5]].

assumptions.text: Existing artifact ids and file names are kept (apart from standalone S001 becoming s1), so references, amendment records and issue links keep working
Only the holder of a unit authors under it, so per-unit counters (diagram numbers) and the rewrite of an artifact's head file do not race across clones
Tracker comments on GitHub and GitLab can be read through the existing gh and glab command paths without a new credential
Union merge of append-only line files is available in the git versions teams use
A repository can be converted in one commit and every clone upgrades together after that commit merges

constraints.text: There is exactly one identity scheme for stored artifacts; the work-item id module is removed and nothing parses the folder key back into an id
An artifact id never changes once created, except the single rename of an uppercase story or task id (S001 to s1) by the s9 conversion
A revision moves only when an artifact's content changes; an identical rewrite, a comment, a reference change or a provenance write does not move it
Feedback entries are immutable and append-only with no state of their own; they are resolved as part of the artifact that is revised
Gates decide on the live identity reported by the tracker, never on a declared alias
A tracker issue is never an artifact; lifecycle artifacts are 1:1 with an issue and supporting artifacts attach to the issue of the unit they describe
Folder names under docs/epics stay as they are today, with the date always taken from the epic's creation time
A completed status is recorded once, when a unit's Tasks or Stories are all complete and its review is clean or explicitly overridden by the user
Cloud access stays through the local CLI binaries; no direct REST providers are added

stories.title: One identity scheme for every artifact
stories.userValue: A person sees the same id for an artifact everywhere: in the repository, in the log, in references and on the tracker, so nothing has to be translated between two schemes.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an existing repository with artifacts named by the current scheme
acceptanceCriteria.when: the second identity scheme is removed
acceptanceCriteria.then: every artifact stored in the lowercase story form keeps its id and file name and keeps resolving, and an artifact stored in the uppercase form (S001) fails with a message that points to the s9 conversion, which renames it once

acceptanceCriteria.given: a new Epic, Story or Task issue is created on the tracker
acceptanceCriteria.then: the title starts with the artifact's id, and an issue created earlier keeps its title and is still found by its unit label

acceptanceCriteria.given: two artifacts of one epic written on different days
acceptanceCriteria.then: both land in the same folder, because the date always comes from the epic's creation time and a folder name is never read back as an id

functionalRequirements.statement: Epics, Stories, Tasks, the Tasks file and diagrams have ids in the same scheme as the existing artifacts.
functionalRequirements.rationale: One scheme for everything that is stored.

functionalRequirements.statement: A story or task is written in one form everywhere.
functionalRequirements.rationale: s1 and S001 must not name two things.

stories.title: A common artifact model with one reader
stories.userValue: Every stored entity has the same basic shape, so a tool, a person or the delivery board reads any of them the same way.

acceptanceCriteria.given: any stored entity of any type
acceptanceCriteria.then: it exposes an identity, a description, an optional parent, references, a change log, feedback and a lifecycle in one shape

acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact type that has no use for a lifecycle part
acceptanceCriteria.then: that part is simply empty and nothing fails

acceptanceCriteria.given: a reference from one artifact to another or to an external thing
acceptanceCriteria.then: it names the target, the kind of thing it is and why the link exists, and the Epic, Story and Task chain is given by each artifact's parent

functionalRequirements.statement: Every stored entity is an artifact with the common fields and its own payload.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Uniformity is the point of the Epic.

functionalRequirements.statement: The children of an artifact are found from the parent link, never stored on the parent.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Nothing is stored that can be derived.

stories.title: A lifecycle that says where an artifact stands
stories.userValue: Anyone can see whether an artifact is a draft, waiting for review, approved, in signoff or completed, and which revision each decision covers.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an approved artifact
acceptanceCriteria.then: its revision moves, its status returns to draft, and the earlier approval and review remain visible as covering the older revision

acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact rewritten with identical content, or given a comment, a reference or a provenance record
acceptanceCriteria.then: its revision does not move

acceptanceCriteria.given: all Tasks of a Story are complete and its build record has been code-reviewed clean or approved by the user over the review's findings
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Story is recorded as completed once, its documents and records complete with it, and the Epic completes when all its Stories have; dropped or superseded children do not count

acceptanceCriteria.given: a head whose content hash does not match its revision
acceptanceCriteria.when: anyone tries to approve, review or complete it
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is reported as a conflict and the action is refused until a person resolves it

functionalRequirements.statement: A lifecycle holds the current revision, approval, review, signoffs and staleness, and a status from a fixed set of ten.
Completion rolls up from Tasks to Stories to Epics and is recorded once.
functionalRequirements.rationale: The claim is released at that moment.

stories.title: Change history and feedback that merge across clones
stories.userValue: A team working in several clones of one repository adds history and feedback without conflicts, and a real conflict is caught instead of silently resolved.

acceptanceCriteria.given: two clones each add different feedback or change log entries to the same artifact
acceptanceCriteria.then: the merge completes with no conflict and a reader sees every entry once, in order

acceptanceCriteria.given: a build, review or test round that is overwritten in place
acceptanceCriteria.then: the change log gains an entry with the round's outcome, so earlier rounds can still be read

acceptanceCriteria.given: an artifact's head changed in two clones
acceptanceCriteria.then: git reports the conflict and a person resolves it

functionalRequirements.statement: An artifact's history and feedback are kept as separate append-only records beside its head.
Counts, open feedback and current status are worked out when read, not stored.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Two clones cannot update them differently.

stories.title: Feedback on any artifact, from people and clients
stories.userValue: A person can leave feedback on a design, a plan or a single Task, reply to feedback, and see what is still open.

acceptanceCriteria.given: any artifact, a Task included
acceptanceCriteria.when: a person adds feedback or a reply
acceptanceCriteria.then: the entry is recorded once with who wrote it and when, and is never edited afterwards

acceptanceCriteria.given: feedback on an artifact that is then revised
acceptanceCriteria.then: that feedback counts as addressed unless the author listed only some entries, and the rest stay open

acceptanceCriteria.given: a person with a tracker account and a different repository host account
acceptanceCriteria.then: each is recorded under a namespaced identity, the person can declare the links between their identities, and gates still use the tracker's own identity

functionalRequirements.statement: Feedback entries have a kind (comment, suggestion or revision request) and may point at a place in the artifact.
functionalRequirements.rationale: A revision request must be distinguishable.

functionalRequirements.statement: Actors are recorded as people, agents or systems with a namespaced id.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Several identity sources must not collide.

stories.title: Tracker binding and attachments
stories.userValue: Every unit people work on is linked to exactly one tracker issue, and the documents that support it are reachable from that issue.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an issue a person created first, or one the framework created
acceptanceCriteria.then: the artifact is bound to that one issue, and a repository with no tracker has no binding

acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan, a design document, a diagram or a build, review or test record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the unit's issue gets a link to the file at the commit that holds it on GitHub or GitLab, a real attachment on Jira, and a new revision adds a new link while the old one stays

acceptanceCriteria.given: a link under a parent issue or a post to an issue that failed
acceptanceCriteria.when: the unit is next worked on
acceptanceCriteria.then: the pending work is retried and not repeated once done

functionalRequirements.statement: A binding holds the issue reference and the bookkeeping of what was posted, as a typed record.
Attachment is an operation each tracker implements in its own way.

stories.title: Tasks as artifacts, created when the plan is approved
stories.userValue: Each Task has its own issue, history, feedback and status from the moment its plan is approved, and the holder can refine a Task without redoing the plan.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a plan that is approved
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Tasks of that Story exist together in one file, each with its own id, and each Task has its issue under the Story's issue

acceptanceCriteria.given: a Task whose summary, size, acceptance checks or tests the holder edits
acceptanceCriteria.then: the Task moves to a new revision and returns to draft, needs the local user's re-approval and no signoff, and the plan keeps its own revision

acceptanceCriteria.given: an edit that would add, drop or reorder Tasks or change what depends on what
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is refused with a pointer to a re-plan

acceptanceCriteria.given: a re-plan that is approved
acceptanceCriteria.when: the Tasks are brought into line
acceptanceCriteria.then: a changed Task gets a new revision, a dropped Task is withdrawn with its issue closed, a new Task takes the next number, and no Task id is ever reused

functionalRequirements.statement: A Task's build rounds are recorded in its own history and it completes when a round passes the gate.

stories.title: Feedback read back from the tracker
stories.userValue: A comment someone writes on a Task's or Story's issue shows up as feedback on that artifact, and feedback entered elsewhere reaches the issue, each once.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a human comment on the unit's issue
acceptanceCriteria.when: the holder starts to implement or validate the Task, or asks for a sync
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is recorded once as feedback with the tracker user as author, and the framework's own posts are never recorded

acceptanceCriteria.given: a comment whose first line asks for a revision or offers a suggestion
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is given that kind, and any other comment is a plain comment

acceptanceCriteria.given: feedback entered against a unit that has an issue
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is posted once and marked as in the tracker, and a later edit or deletion on the tracker is not mirrored

functionalRequirements.statement: Reading comments needs no background polling and no new credential.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Reads happen where the holder works on the unit.

stories.title: Upfront conversion of a repository
stories.userValue: A team converts a repository to the new model once, safely, and the delivery board and every tool see one consistent shape afterwards.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository with artifacts of every existing type
acceptanceCriteria.then: every artifact is converted in one commit, Epics, Stories and Tasks are created for what exists, statuses are computed, and the change log is filled in from what the artifacts already record, marked as migrated

acceptanceCriteria.given: a conversion that is run again, or run as a preview
acceptanceCriteria.then: a repeat changes nothing, a preview changes nothing and lists what would change, and a verification reads the result back through the delivery reader and reports any difference

acceptanceCriteria.given: a repository that has not been converted
acceptanceCriteria.when: the new tools run on it
acceptanceCriteria.then: they refuse with a clear message to convert it first; builds from before this model are not expected to work with a converted repository

functionalRequirements.statement: Conversion is a single command that previews, repeats safely and verifies itself.
